summary: A topic guide using Keenan Cornelius’s published lapel-denial discussion to identify what a lapel player needs before an entry can develop.
description: Read the passer’s side of lapel engagement to organize questions about your own lapel-guard setup.
overview: The selected article explains lapel entry from the passer’s perspective. For the guard player, it offers a way to distinguish having a lapel grip from having the fabric and leg access needed to develop an entanglement.

guide.display_title: Lapel Guard: Study the Entry Obstacles

fits: You can reach a lapel but cannot tell why the intended guard entry remains unavailable.
consider_alternative_if: For a guard curriculum organized around two sleeve grips and lasso/spider configurations, compare Jonathan Thomas’s guide.

includes: The article separates taking slack out of the lapel, approaching outside the legs and using a foot-control grip.
Its first section explicitly distinguishes merely holding the lapel from freeing enough fabric for an entry.
limits: This selected source concerns denying entry; it is not a full account of worm, squid or their sweep sequences.

start_here.title: Compare a lapel grip with usable lapel length
start_here.task: Read Tip #1 and compare the article’s description of one freed lapel with its description of freeing both. In your study notes, separate possession of the grip from available fabric length. Then read Tip #2 and note why the passer’s approach may prevent the bottom player from using that grip.
start_here.section: Tip #1: Take Slack Out The Lapel

sources.title: How To Pass Lapel Guards: Keenan Finally Comes Clean — Cristiano Del Giacco
sources.note: Read the public Jiu Jitsu X article presenting Keenan Cornelius’s lapel-denial concepts: available lapel slack, outside positioning and the calamari grip. Embedded demonstrations not reviewed.

sources.title: Double Sleeve Guard by Jonathan Thomas
sources.note: Verified basic control, De La Riva, lasso/spider defenses, Spider-X and opponent-posture sections. Listing inspected; course video content not reviewed.

flashcards.question: Does holding an opponent’s lapel alone establish a lapel-guard entry?
flashcards.answer: No. The Jiu Jitsu X article distinguishes having the grip from freeing enough lapel length to enter the position.
flashcards.answer_line: The grip also needs usable slack.
